text:
omar: Heads up — after the merge of r/core#3456 I'm seeing a compile storm on canary. p95 token latency +18%, compile-queue depth spiked, and kvcache eviction rate jumped. :boom:

jess: Ugh. Which commit? any obvious churn to autotune/selector?

omar: commit 9f3b2a1c changed autotune tie-break logic (seed update). It looks like small-batch int8 short-seq cases are now picking a different kernel variant and triggering a ton of new kernels to compile. Lots of cache invalidation.

leah: Snapshot from perf VM (short summary):
```
- host: canary-3
- peak compile queue: 62 -> normally 6
- median compile time: 120ms -> 70ms
- observed selector picks: variant_a (old) -> variant_c (new fallback)
- kvcache churn: evictions/sec x3
```

leah: The selector's tiebreak seed flip means requests that used to reuse existing compiled kernels now route to a variant that isn't cached. That explodes compile parallelism and thrashes kvcache.

jess: CI perf run also flagged this. @ci-bot do we have the job link?

ci-bot: perf/regression job: https://ci.internal/reports/2298765 — baseline vs HEAD shows 12% regression on short-chat workload, compile queue backlog +950% :warning:

release-manager: Please hold the canary rollout until this is understood. Marking rollout:hold. :hand:

omar: Agree. I propose two immediate mitigations:
1) Flip runtime flag to force previous tie-break behavior: `runtime.autopick_seed=legacy` (hotfix config)
2) Add compile concurrency cap on canary nodes to throttle storm while we bisect.

jess: I'll run a quick bisect across the autotune PRs. Starting with r/core commits around 9f3b2a1c -> will narrow to the change. Expected time ~30-45m.

leah: For the bisect: focus on the small-batch short-seq path and also monitor `kvcache_hits`/`evictions` and `compile_success_rate`. If we can reproduce locally, we can avoid full cluster rollbacks.

jess: Early bisect result: flip shows the heuristic change at r/core#3456 is the culprit — seed change swapped priority of kernel candidates. Confirmed on repro with synthetic short-seq workload.

omar: Given that, I'm going to push the flag flip to canary and block further merges to main that touch autotune until we ship a safer tiebreak (or add stability hashing to the selector).

leah: Also opening a follow-up PR to make autotune picks stable across small nondeterministic changes: add deterministic fallback order + metrics to detect new kernel churn. PR: r/core#3468.

jess: I've posted a brief incident note in #incidents and flagged the PRs. Once the hotfix is in, we'll rerun perf jobs and decide on a revert vs patch.

omar: Thanks all. Actions:
- @release-manager keep rollout on hold
- @jess finish bisect + hotfix deploy (runtime.autopick_seed=legacy)
- @leah open the stability PR and add perf tests for short-seq kernel churn
- @perf-bot schedule perf run in 20m

perf-bot: scheduled: perf/regression in 20m -> will post results.

release-manager: Noted. If hotfix doesn't fix perf we'll revert r/core#3456.

jess: Hotfix deployed to canary (flag flipped). Early telemetry shows compile queue dropping and p95 improving. Will wait for full perf run. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: perf/regression result: compile-queue backlog down to 8 (from 62), p95 delta now +1.5% vs baseline.

omar: Good. Keep the hold until PR 3468 lands with tests. We'll do a controlled rollout with the new stable-pick behavior.

leah: I'll add a short e2e in CI that simulates churn and asserts kernel-reuse ratio doesn't regress >5%.

jess: Thanks team — incident closed once 3468 merges and we unflag.

release-manager: closing the hold after merge + green perf job.
